title: The TOADALNAEC and the Three Lies
subtitle: Waluigi's Cut — a free mask, a ship with two names, a gold handshake, three lies on a scorecard, one 'oopsie' and a speaker who left his hands in his pockets
filed: 2 Aethel, 1040 BF — the morning after, from the screening desk, by someone who was not on the ship
pullQuote: 'Get away from me, you filth animal. Surround her. Oh, oopsie.' OOPSIE. Waluigi has been keeping that for the encore.
standfirst: The tape is a shop, a gangway, a song and a hall, and Waluigi has the projector warm and his hand on the pause button. Contains: a free mask from a shop that pays a third, a boat with the same layout and a different name, a toad who asked a stranger if she was solid, a recruitment song with a bullet in it, three lies recited from a lesson plan, a speaker who put his hands in his pockets to prove he had used them, a tea service, a truth spell, and a duel the crowd walked out of.

sections.heading: STOP THE TAPE: THE SHOP IS GIVING SOMETHING AWAY
sections.body:
Waluigi has the projector warm and the lights down, and the first thing on the reel is a counter. WAH. A SHOP counter. The same shop that, this very morning, looked at a bar of gold worth fifty and said *fifteen.* The same shopkeeper. The same face. And on this tape that same face comes out from behind the counter and says, to Remi, with NO prompting, **"I have an adventure mask for you, and it's free."**

Freeze it. Waluigi would like the room to look at the shopkeeper's hands. He is giving a thing away. This is a man who pays a third of what anything is worth and then charges you for the third.

Remi's response is, and Waluigi will defend this to anyone, a perfect piece of consumer behaviour. **"For free? It does sound interesting. For free."** *For free.* She said it twice. She said it the way a person says a word they have never been permitted to use.

He hands it over. The tape describes it as *gloomy.* That is the whole description. Not cursed, not old, not ominous. Gloomy, like a Tuesday. And Remi, who has just turned a mask over once in her hands, says the most sensible thing anybody says all afternoon: **"I won't wear it. Maybe the toads will."**

Roll it on.

Waluigi would like to log a formal complaint on behalf of the toads. Nobody asked the toads. The mask was offered to a person and passed to a *species,* and the species was not in the room. WAH. Green T, from the door, delivers the line that every one of these parties needs and none of them has ever kept: **"I better supervise them."**

He did not supervise them. Keep watching.

sections.heading: "IT MAY BE THE SAME LAYOUT": A DISPUTE OVER A BOAT
sections.body:
The party walks up to the old Vigilance singing, which is the correct way to approach a boat you used to own, and a gate toad puts his hand up.

Waluigi has been through a LOT of gates. Legion gates, baton gates, a gate with a doctor on it holding a bone saw. This is the first one guarded by a toad who has been briefed on the *legal position,* and WAH, it is magnificent.

**"Us. The owners of the airship."**

**"That's not right."**

**"What do you mean it's ours?"**

**"No, no, no, no. This is the TOADS' airship. The TOADALNAEC. It belongs to Speaker Rivers."**

Now Waluigi has been saying that word for an hour. TOADALNAEC. It does not scan. It is nine syllables of somebody running out of ship. The Legion called it the Legionlance, which was already a crime against the language, and the Toads took one look and said *we can do worse,* and they were RIGHT.

Pause the tape on the next line, because it is the best line in the filing and nobody on the tape knows it. **"No, no, it may be the same layout, but I assure you it's ours."**

THE SAME LAYOUT. They are not arguing about whether it is the Vigilance. Both sides have agreed it is the Vigilance. They have agreed on the hull, the gangway, the rails and the smell. The only open question is the *name on the door,* and the gate toad answers it the way every bureaucrat in this archive answers every question: **"Come on out, Hudston. We have a problem."**

He sent for HUDSTON. WAH.

sections.heading: GOLD OR GOLD-PLATED: THE HANDSHAKE THAT BECAME A TRADITION
sections.body:
Hudston walks out and the first thing he says to a stranger on his deck is **"Wow, are you gold or gold-plated?"**

That is a toad with no sense of occasion. Waluigi has been in the same room as very senior people and has never once asked one if they were solid.

Remi's answer is the best deflection on the reel. **"Come and find out for yourself."** She holds out a hand. He shakes it. He is gold.

*GOLD.* From the palm up. He looks at himself, he turns to the gangway and he announces, with real joy, **"Hey, guys, check it out. I'm gold now."** Green T's contribution is to ask him to stand against a wall and fire a gun at him. WAH. The bullet bounces off. Hudston's review of the experience: **"How can I ever repay you? It kinda stung, but it's really fun."**

Four stars. *Would be shot again.* And Green T shoots again, because Green T is a professional and a second sample is good practice.

Now the toads on the gangway, who have been watching this with the faces of men at a magic show, say the sentence that opens the second half of the tape: **"You're one of the toads now."**

Remi starts singing. **"Oh, I'm the new toad, listen to me, I'll sing a song in the air or the sea."** The toads sing it back. They pick her UP. It is the only recruitment ceremony Waluigi has ever approved of, because it contains a gold toad, a bullet, and a chorus.

And the tape shows the Disaster Inc. toads running after her to *save* her. She is being carried on shoulders, singing. She does not need saving. Rank it: Remi, 10. Rescue party, 2.

sections.heading: THE SCORECARD: THE THREE LIES OF ARCHIE MISER, GRADED
sections.body:
Waluigi has the pen out. A hall of toads has produced a lesson plan and the lesson plan has numbers on it. Grade it.

**Lie one: "He saved the toads."** The correction, from the crowd: *No, he put them back in their place, to be cogs in the machine.* Grade: C. It has the structure of an argument, it has a tone of righteous anger, and it comes from a hall full of toads who are standing up, unchained, in a flying ship. WAH.

**Lie two: "Archie Miser is a sane individual."** The correction: *False. He burnt down a village full of orphans.* And Archie, from a barrel, answers it in the best line of the afternoon: **"I do have flaws, but the village never happened. On remembering, it was someone else."** Grade: A for the denial and F for the denial, simultaneously. Waluigi will be thinking about *on remembering* for a week.

**Lie three: "Anything Archie says is a lie."** Grade: A+. It is the cleverest thing in the hall, because it disqualifies the answer to lies one and two before the answer is given. A man cannot rebut it. He can only say *that's a lie,* and then it is proved. WAH. Somebody in that ship went to school.

And then Markop pokes the one hole in the whole programme, which is **"Why isn't he fireballing us right now?"** The answer, from Rivers: **"Because he is scared of me."** Archie, from the barrel, with a barrel's gravity: **"This is the first time I've met you. You don't scare me at all."**

Then the one serious beat on the tape. **"I need to understand why you hate me. I saved you guys, all 150 of you. So why?"**

Nobody answers him. WAH.

sections.heading: OOPSIE, AND THE HANDS IN THE POCKETS
sections.body:
Archie says **"Take it away, Remi,"** which is a deeply optimistic thing to say to Remi, who responds with **"I'm not sure why Archie is evil, but why not?"** and goes for a high five. UP HIGH. Rivers dodges it.

And then the line. The line Waluigi has been keeping for the encore. **"Get away from me, you filth animal. Surround her. Oh, oopsie."**

*OOPSIE.* He said *filth animal* to a girl standing in a hall full of his own recruits, and the whole hall heard him say it, and in the half a second between the insult and the *oopsie,* the whole hall heard what the Speaker calls them when he thinks they cannot hear. Markop, to his eternal credit, does the thing: **"You guys want to be called that?"** WAH. The toads pause.

Now watch the follow-up, because Markop has found the thread and pulls it. **"Did anyone actually see Speaker Rivers fight?"** **"Yeah, I fought. Killed them with my bare hands."** He puts his hands in his pockets.

*In his pockets.* Waluigi has seen a great many liars and not one of them has ever hidden the evidence by *leaving it in his trousers.*

**"Let me see your hands. They should be bruised and bloodied."** Nothing. **"Out of your pockets."** He does a fake trip. He lands on the floor. He comes up showing both palms. **"See? My hands are dirty. Dirt and dust."**

**"I said bruised and bloodied."**

And then his best defence. **"I personally unchained you guys."** **"Does anyone remember being unchained by him?"** **"The metaphorical chains."** And a toad, in the crowd, says: **"Makes sense."**

Waluigi had no reply to that either.

sections.heading: THE TEA SERVICE AND THE SPELL THAT WORKED ON THE WRONG TOAD
sections.body:
Rivers is *tired.* He needs to be carried. He is lifted onto toad shoulders, like a man in a procession, and somebody says **"Your tea's ready, sir."** Markop, who has his suspicions about the cup, asks the question: **"That's not a potion, is it?"** **"No, no. Just tea."**

Then Markop opens his spellbook and smiles, and Waluigi would like the camera to hold on that smile, because it is the one real moment of menace in a filing that has otherwise run on songs and tea. **"We don't have to fight. You just have to tell the truth, and I'll go. I have a spell that will make it so you can't lie."**

Meanwhile, to the side: Remi, bored, leans on a toad. Gold. She yawns and swats another. Gold. She kicks her legs back and a third toad goes gold. WAH. She has made three solid-gold toads in a hall in the time it took Markop to read a paragraph, and she has not looked up from her own boredom once. That is a CAREER.

Back to the tea. **"Of course I'd never lie to anyone."** Markop: **"Now say the truth spell didn't work."** Rivers: **"Maybe you're a bad magician."** The spell, it turns out, did not land on Rivers. It landed on the toad next to him.

**"Tell me your secret."**

**"I like lifting up people, and I also stole something from Archi—"**

And Rivers forces the tea down his throat. The toad throws up. **"Hey, what did he steal?"** **"Into the dungeon with him."**

A blue coffee, after. The question of what he stole is still open, and the case is in the dungeon.

sections.heading: THE PEN IS MIGHTIER, AND THE CROWD GOES HOME
sections.body:
Markop is, by now, out of patience and into his best rhythm. **"You're lying. We need to duel. The spell clearly didn't work."** **"I am the best. It's not a lie."**

Archie is still in his barrel. Waluigi would like to say this once more so it is on the tape: *Archie is still in the barrel.* He is the cause of the whole dispute, he is the subject of the lesson, and he has been parked, patiently, at the side of the room like luggage.

And then the weapon, the most Toad thing on the reel: Rivers attacks Markop with a PEN. **"The pen is mightier than the sword."** He said it. Waluigi has no further comment on it.

The duel goes in the order in which these things go. Markop attacks. Rivers catches fire and screams. A battleaxe comes round and catches fire and he screams again. **"AAAA."** Markop swings and misses. Somebody grabs for the axe and is too weak to take it. WAH. The tape does not say whose hands, and Waluigi has played it back four times.

Then the best detail of all. The toads start walking out. **"Lame."** **"He is losing his crowd."** They *leave.* In the middle of a fight, they have decided the Speaker is boring.

And Markop smiles and prepares for another strike.

Waluigi ends the reel there, because the account does too. A man on fire, a centaur with a smile, a barrel in the corner, and a hall that has stopped believing. Roll credits. WAH.
